title: DoorDash to Acquire Instacart for $17 Billion in Massive Grocery Delivery Push
snippet: DoorDash announced a $17 billion deal to buy Instacart, creating a delivery giant aimed at competing directly with Walmart and Amazon in the hyper-local grocery market.
content:
In a blockbuster move aimed at reshaping the digital retail landscape, DoorDash announced Thursday that it has agreed to acquire grocery delivery provider Instacart in a deal valued at $17 billion.

The acquisition signals a major expansion for San Francisco-based DoorDash, which has aggressively moved beyond restaurant takeout to capture a larger share of the fast-growing hyper-local delivery market. Under the terms of the agreement, DoorDash will pay $65 per Instacart share—a 26% premium over the stock’s Oct. 22 closing price. The transaction consists of 75% cash, with Instacart stockholders given the option to receive cash, DoorDash stock, or a combination of both. Instacart's board of directors has unanimously approved the deal.

Targeting E-Commerce Heavyweights

The aggressive consolidation comes as retail giants Walmart and Amazon continue to expand their hold on same-day and fast-turnaround grocery delivery. According to estimates from Wedbush, Walmart currently leads the online grocery segment with a 30.9% market share, followed by Amazon at 23.6%.

By combining DoorDash’s logistics network with Instacart’s established network of supermarket partnerships, the combined entity hopes to build a powerful counterweight against the two retail giants.

"Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online," DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in a statement. "Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery."

What It Means for Consumers and Merchants

To win over consumers, DoorDash indicated that users will eventually benefit from bundled membership perks, essentially giving subscribers access to two platforms for the price of one. The company noted that Instacart shoppers will gain access to more than 50,000 additional merchant locations on top of the nearly 100,000 retail stores already available on Instacart's app.

For local couriers and gig workers, the company stated that the unified platform will offer broader opportunities to earn across both restaurant and retail deliveries.

Wall Street initial reaction was mixed following the announcement: DoorDash stock surged over 5% in premarket trading, while Instacart shares traded slightly lower.
